topic: Sahasrabudhe's even additive-complexity construction question for finite morphisms of universal words
title: Parity in Sahasrabudhe's additive-complexity question: extending Banero's morphism criterion

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: For the even-complexity construction question posed by Sahasrabudhe in Sturmian Words and Constant Additive Complexity (2015, Section 5, p. 7), we extend Banero's common-slope criterion (2013, Theorem 21): a bounded-complexity finite-morphic image of a word containing every finite source word has odd additive complexity at every sufficiently large multiple of the codeword-length gcd, by pairing complementary factor sums. Empty codewords are allowed when the output is infinite; consequently an eventually constant positive complexity is odd. Equal sums of equal-length complete images and complementary windows give a reflection with one fixed point. The argument also applies to lattice-valued sums, including abelian complexity. We give the anchored-word consequence of Banero's criterion and show that uniformly recurrent outputs are periodic.
summary: A complementary-factor involution gives eventual odd cardinality at gcd-admissible lengths for bounded lattice-valued complexity of universal-input finite-morphic images. Scalar consequences include the negative answer to Sahasrabudhe's even-complexity construction question. Further written consequences concern common slopes, anchored words and periodicity under uniform recurrence.

coverage.statement: Bounded complexity gives odd cardinality at all sufficiently large multiples of the gcd of codeword lengths
Eventually constant positive additive complexity is odd
A uniformly recurrent infinite output is periodic; a constant-complexity such output is constant
Other uniformly recurrent fixed-complexity constructions outside this universal-input method
Bounded complexity is equivalent to common average among nonempty codewords; the output is anchored, giving the universal-input special case of Banero's Problem 32
